thread:
alex_m: heads up — running the new eval harness sweep (temp 0.3..1.2, top_k 10/40/100) and seeing nondeterministic splits in outputs even with a fixed global seed.

tasha: hmm — nondet across runs or across workers within the same run? :eyes:

alex_m: within same run across different requests routed to different workers. seed is fixed at test kickoff.

samir: do you seed per-worker at startup or per-request? we had a similar thing where worker-id bucketized RNG streams.

alex_m: we seed at worker startup: seed_worker = base_seed ^ worker_index; so every worker gets a disjoint stream.

jin-ops: that pattern is normally fine. what's the sampling algorithm? top_k or top_p? any quantized kernel involved?

alex_m: top_k sampler with temperature scaling. the model is quantized int8; kernel is the new fused topk+multinomial path.

alex_m: short repro snippet I ran locally:
```python
base_seed = 12345
for w in range(num_workers):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(base_seed ^ w)
    # sampler uses rng.choice after argpartition
    samples = sampler.sample(logits, rng)
```

tasha: small thought — argpartition + picking ties can depend on numeric jitter from quantized kernels; if the topk cutoff moves slightly it can flip which tokens are inside the top_k.

samir: also the C++ sampler uses std::mt19937 seeded with (uint32_t)seed; truncating a 64-bit base seed can cause collisions if we xor with worker id. collisions -> effectively same stream for multiple workers.

alex_m: interesting — when I forced top_k to 100 the buckets merged and runs were consistent. at top_k=40 I get two clusters of outputs and the clusters map 1:1 to worker ids.

jin-ops: can you paste a tiny log of token ids from two different workers? even 3-4 tokens will tell if order difference is from sampling or minor logits change.

alex_m: pasted logs:
```
worker0: [12, 87, 5, 202, 11]
worker1: [12, 87, 9, 202, 11]
worker2: [12, 87, 5, 202, 11]
``` 
notice token 3 differs (5 vs 9) only when top_k=40 and temp=0.9

eva: my quick hunch: two causes compounding — (1) quantized kernel numeric jitter causes rank cutoff to move, (2) rng seeding truncation / per-worker seeding produces different discrete streams; when cutoff is near the end of top_k, those small differences map to a different sampler distribution => apparent nondet.

samir: mitigation ideas:
- use per-request RNG seeded with a 64-bit hash of (base_seed, request_id) rather than per-worker startup seeds
- avoid truncating to 32-bit when seeding C++ mt19937; use std::mt19937_64 or seeding routine that expands
- add a deterministic tie-breaker in argpartition (stable sort on token id)

tasha: agree. second point: add a unit test that sweeps (seed, top_k, temperature) and asserts identical outputs across worker_count variations (1 vs N workers) for a small fixed set of logits.

alex_m: I tried per-request seeding with hashlib.blake2b(seed_bytes + request_id).digest() -> int64 and it made the outputs stable across workers for my local test.

jin-ops: can you open a PR with the per-request seeding and the test? also please include a flag to opt-in to legacy per-worker startup seeding so we can roll back quickly.

ci-bot: CI triggered: test/eval_runner/determinism_grid — job #2167

eva: small code suggestion (pseudo):
```cpp
// replace truncation
uint64_t s64 = hash64(base_seed, request_id);
std::mt19937_64 rng(s64);
// or use splitmix64 to seed a per-request stream
```

samir: and make sampler.choice use rng.uniform_int(0, UINT64_MAX) instead of modulo of a truncated 32-bit value — avoids bias.

alex_m: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4823 — includes per-request seeding + deterministic tie-breaker in topk path + unit test covering top_k=[10,40,100] temp=[0.5,0.9]

tasha: nice. please add a note in the PR description about the quantized kernel jitter explanation so reviewers know why the change is needed.

jin-ops: after the PR lands let's run the staging eval grid for a couple thousand examples — if outputs are stable across replicas we can backport to the quantize/rc branch.

alex_m: quick local results after patch: deterministic across 1/4/8 workers for the earlier failing prompts. logs attached in PR.

eva: add a dashboard test in the eval runner that flags when the same seed produces >1 distinct clusters of outputs across workers (we can treat cluster count > 1 as flaky).

samir: +1 — that will help CI catch regressions from future kernel changes.

alex_m: thanks everyone. merging to staging now. :party_parrot:

ci-bot: job #2167 passed — determinism_grid OK :white_check_mark:

jin-ops: great — let's monitor the next quantization rollout. assigning follow-up ticket to eng-ml/backlog.
